title: Advertising Code for Intermediaries
text: Advertisements and client communications must not state or imply that returns are guaranteed, assured or risk-free. Any reference to past performance must be accompanied by the statement that past performance is not a reliable indicator of future results.

title: Guidelines on Deposit Product Advertising
text: Regulated entities shall not describe deposit or investment products as risk-free. Claims about returns must be accurate, balanced and supported by the terms of the product.

title: Research Analyst Communication Standards
text: Forward-looking statements in research reports must be clearly labelled as estimates or projections and must disclose the material assumptions on which they are based.

title: Insurance Product Communication Guidelines
text: Insurers and distributors shall not present indicative benefit illustrations as guaranteed outcomes. Illustrations must be shown at the prescribed rates together with a clear statement that benefits are not guaranteed.

title: Disclosure of Past Performance
text: Where past performance is displayed, the scheme or portfolio, the period covered, the benchmark and the warning that past performance is not indicative of future results must all be disclosed with equal prominence.

title: Risk Disclosure in Offer Documents
text: Offer documents and product notes must prominently disclose the risk factors, including the possibility of loss of capital. Risk disclosures must not be buried in footnotes or omitted from marketing summaries.

title: Product Riskometer Requirements
text: Product literature for mutual funds and portfolio strategies must display the prescribed riskometer and a capital-at-risk warning on the front page of the document.

title: Structured Product Suitability and Disclosure
text: Marketing material for structured products must state that capital is at risk and explain any conditions that could reduce or eliminate returns, including early redemption and counterparty risks.

title: Insurance Product Risk Disclosure
text: Product summaries must disclose surrender value risk, lapse consequences and any charges that reduce the maturity benefit. The disclosure must be in plain language and in the same document as the benefit illustration.

title: Mutual Fund Scheme Risk Statement
text: All scheme advertisements and one-pagers must carry the statement that investments are subject to market risks and that investors should read all scheme-related documents carefully before investing.

title: Disclosure of Total Expense Ratio
text: Intermediaries must disclose the total expense ratio and all recurring charges applicable to a product in the client communication. Indirect charges must be identified as such.

title: Total Cost Disclosure for Investment Products
text: A complete, itemised table of all entry, ongoing and exit charges must be provided to the client before the investment is made. The table must state each charge as an amount and as a percentage of the investment.

title: Performance Fee Disclosure
text: Where a performance fee applies, the rate, the calculation method, the benchmark and the frequency of crystallisation must be disclosed in the product document. Fees may not be described as 'available on request'.

title: Transparent Customer Charges
text: Regulated entities must publish a tariff schedule listing all charges applicable to customer accounts and must not levy any charge that is not disclosed in that schedule.

title: Disclosure of Distribution Commission
text: Distribution commissions and trail fees paid to intermediaries must be disclosed to the client in monetary terms at the time of the recommendation and in the periodic account statement.

title: Insurance Charge Disclosure
text: Insurers must show every charge deducted from the policy fund, including allocation, administration, mortality and surrender charges, in the policy document and in the annual statement.

title: Master Direction - Know Your Customer
text: Before establishing a business relationship, a regulated entity shall complete customer due diligence, including verification of identity and source of funds, and shall maintain the records of that verification.

title: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (Revised)
text: Regulated entities must verify identity using a valid officially valid document and record the source of funds before activating an account. Enhanced due diligence is required for high-risk customers, politically exposed persons and beneficial owners.

title: Beneficial Ownership Identification
text: Regulated entities must identify the beneficial owner of every account and verify that ownership before processing transactions above the prescribed threshold.

title: Politically Exposed Person Screening
text: Customers and beneficial owners must be screened against politically exposed person and sanctions lists at onboarding and on an ongoing basis. Screening results must be retained in the client file.

title: Source of Funds for Third-Party Transfers
text: Where funds are received from a third party, the regulated entity must obtain and verify the source of funds and record the relationship between the account holder and the remitter before crediting the account.

title: KYC Requirements for Securities Market Intermediaries
text: Intermediaries must complete know-your-customer verification before executing the first transaction and must not defer identity verification until after funds have been accepted.

title: Suitability and Appropriateness Assessment
text: Before recommending a product, an intermediary must assess the client's risk tolerance, investment horizon and objectives, and must record why the recommendation is suitable for that profile.

title: Client Risk Profiling Standards
text: Risk profiling must use an objective questionnaire, be reviewed at least annually and be updated when the client's circumstances change. A recommendation that conflicts with the recorded profile must be explained in writing.

title: Suitability of Deposit and Investment Products
text: Regulated entities must consider the customer's risk profile and investment objective before marketing complex or market-linked products and must not recommend such products to customers seeking capital preservation.

title: Insurance Product Suitability
text: Distributors must assess the prospect's needs, affordability and existing coverage before recommending a policy. The suitability assessment must be documented and retained.

title: Leveraged and Complex Product Restrictions
text: Leveraged, derivative-linked and other complex products must not be recommended to first-time investors or to clients whose recorded risk tolerance is low, unless the client has received independent advice.

title: Data Retention and Customer Consent
text: Regulated entities shall collect only the customer data necessary for the relationship, obtain consent for sharing it with third parties and retain it only for the period required by law.

title: Data Protection and Customer Consent (Revised)
text: Customer data must be encrypted in transit and at rest, access must be role-based and logged, and third-party sharing requires a recorded, purpose-specific consent that the customer can withdraw. Retention periods must be documented in the privacy notice.

title: Digital Personal Data Protection Principles
text: Personal data may be processed only for a lawful purpose with the consent of the data principal. The data fiduciary must give notice of the purpose, retain data only as long as necessary and implement reasonable security safeguards.

title: Cybersecurity and Data Security Framework
text: Intermediaries must protect client records with encryption, access controls and audit logs, and must not transmit identity documents over unencrypted channels such as ordinary email.

title: Retention Limits for Personal Data
text: Personal data must not be retained indefinitely. Records must be deleted or irreversibly anonymised once the purpose of processing is fulfilled and the statutory retention period has expired.

title: Sharing of Policyholder Data
text: Policyholder data may be shared with marketing partners only after obtaining specific consent and must be governed by a written data sharing agreement that records the purpose and retention period.

title: Maintenance of Customer Records
text: Regulated entities shall maintain records of customer instructions, advice and transactions for at least five years from the date of the transaction or the end of the relationship, whichever is later.

title: Maintenance of Customer and Advice Records
text: Regulated entities must retain records of customer instructions, advice, suitability assessments and transactions for at least eight years. Records must be retrievable within the time specified by the supervisor.

title: Record Keeping for Investment Advice
text: Investment advisers must maintain records of the advice given, the basis for the recommendation and the client's instructions for at least five years and must produce them on request.

title: Policy and Advice Record Retention
text: Insurers and distributors must retain policy records, proposal documents and advice for the period prescribed by the regulator and must not destroy records that are subject to an investigation.

title: Recording of Telephone Advice
text: Where investment or product advice is given over the telephone, a contemporaneous record or recording must be made and retained in the client file. Undocumented verbal advice is not an acceptable record.
